atoms.b: Beowulf is one of the earliest examples of Old English poetry, dating back to the ((++700s 1700s)).
It was either sung or spoken with music, and there is only one original ((++written filmed)) copy of it left today: a 1,000-year-old manuscript with over 3,000 lines!

atoms.text: The poem is set in Scandinavia and tells the story of a warrior called Beowulf, who fights three monsters. The first is a troll-like monster called Grendel, who is terrorising the Danes. Beowulf pulls off Grendel’s arm, and the monster flees to his home in the marshes, where he dies.
After Grendel’s mother finds out, she takes her revenge and kills one of the Danes. Beowulf tracks her to her lair and cuts her head off with a sword.

Later on in the poem, Beowulf becomes king. Fifty years after his last battle, a dragon attacks because the treasure it was protecting was stolen. Beowulf kills the dragon to protect his people but is wounded during the fight and dies. The poem ends with Beowulf’s funeral, where his ashes are buried with treasure.

atoms.a: How many monsters did Beowulf fight?

atoms.b: By looking at Beowulf, we can see what values were ((++important boring)) in Anglo-Saxon culture.

For example, Beowulf represents the values of the ((++Heroic Villain)) Code, which included bravery, honour and sacrifice. Although the poem is ((++fictional true)), it tells us that these characteristics were valued in real life.

atoms.a: It was beaten gold, princely headgear hooped and hasped by a weapon-smith who had worked wonders in days gone by and adorned it with boar- shapes; since then it had resisted every sword.

instruction.text: Which two things do you think the boar on the helmet represents?

atoms.b: Anglo-Saxons believed the ((++boar unicorn)) would protect the person wearing the helmet in battle.
Although the poem is a work of fiction, real ((++helmets shoes)) with boars on them have been found. This means that we can use the poem to learn about ((++Anglo-Saxon Roman)) culture and beliefs.
